source.title: Glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors on mortality and hospitalization in heart failure patients: a comprehensive meta-analysis

findings.finding: The article says the 15 included RCTs contain 28,484 participants, but the 15 sample sizes printed in Table 1 sum to 21,808, a difference of 6,676.

Figures 2 and 3 use each Table 1 study sample size as the denominator in both the treatment and control columns. Across the 15 rows, the printed per-arm denominators sum to 43,616, exactly twice the 21,808 Table 1 total.
The abstract and Results report pooled all-cause mortality HR 0.86 with 95% CI 0.79 to 0.92. Figure 2 prints HR 0.86 with 95% CI 0.83 to 0.89.
Supplementary Table S1 says only seven listed studies contributed all-cause mortality and eight contributed HF hospitalization, while Figures 2 and 3 include all 15 studies for both outcomes.
Supplementary Table S1 uses Ganguly 2024 for the DELIVER-like row and Dougherty 2023 for the post-MI row. Main Table 1 uses Verma 2020 and Kotit 2023 in those positions.

The included-study list cites Mordi 2017 as a trial protocol and Ferreira 2025 as a design paper, yet Table 1 and the primary forest plots assign them completed-trial characteristics and mortality or hospitalization event data.
The NT-proBNP Results text says 11 RCTs contributed data, Figure 4 plots 10 study rows, and Supplementary Table S1 maps nine rows to NT-proBNP.
The LVEF Results text and Figure 5 use 10 studies, while Supplementary Table S1 maps only five rows to LVEF, LV systolic function, reverse remodeling, or an LV-function surrogate.
The Results text describes follow-up as 6 to 36 months. Table 1 contains a 3-month minimum and a 28-month maximum.
The risk-of-bias prose reports 10 low-risk trials and five trials described as moderate-risk categories. Table 2 prints 13 overall Low ratings and two Some concerns ratings.
The study-selection prose says 30 articles were included from 45 potentially relevant records and then says 30 were excluded. Figure 1 instead shows 30 full-text exclusions and 15 included studies.
The Results discuss SOGALDI-PEF and DAPA-ICG, but neither name appears in Table 1 or Supplementary Table S1.

The trim-and-fill paragraph says the method altered a pooled HR of 0.86 without major changes and then gives 0.79 to 0.92, which is formatted like the original confidence interval rather than a clearly reported adjusted estimate.

schema_gaps: The LiteratureAtom schema is oriented toward primary literature. This source is a systematic review and meta-analysis, so included-study rows are preserved as secondary-reported study characteristics rather than promoted to primary-study results.
The schema has no dedicated meta-analysis, pooled-result, risk-of-bias, or certainty-of-evidence object. Those concepts are represented with existing atom kinds and descriptive tags.
Cross-source contradictions between main text, figures, tables, bibliography, and Supplementary Table S1 are reported in validation and SEA rather than silently reconciled.
extraction_limitations: Bibliography entries were not atomized. They were exported to the reference task queue.
All atoms remain needs_review because no human source-verification step is represented.
No external bibliographic correction was performed because @VERIFY was not activated.
Calculated source-consistency atoms are limited to arithmetic that can be reproduced directly from printed tables.
